feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-focused roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and overstuffed with overlapping skills sections, which reduces impact and scannability.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within NACo strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good use of scale and scope: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add impact.  
- Strong positioning for modern digital roles: combines strategy, CMS/platform expertise, analytics, governance, and multimedia well.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance where possible.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. other non-serial-comma usage); “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization looks stylistically inconsistent unless intentional.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with sharper specificity, a more distinctive value proposition, and less overlap with the skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and fix style: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience.”
- Lead with current senior positioning and sector relevance: digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Add 1–2 concrete differentiators already supported by the CV, such as enterprise web transformation, cross-functional governance, or translating policy into accessible content.
- Reduce generic lists of channels (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) in favor of outcomes and leadership scope.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, editorial governance, and the systems that enable coordinated communications at scale. Strong background in advocacy and public-sector messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, more senior phrasing: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” and “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership” instead of “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination.”
- Reduce overlap with technical/tool sections by focusing on capability areas, e.g.: Digital transformation strategy • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS governance • Editorial workflow & content operations • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process design • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Standardize style: use either “communication” or “communications” consistently; “communications” fits the rest of the CV better.
- Consider dropping one lower-priority item to keep the list tighter and more executive-level.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “Policy & advocacy communication,” and stakeholder coordination repeat language already covered in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Web & CMS administration” may undersell experience already presented as platform modernization, governance, and enterprise web leadership.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the footer project highlights and prior NACo web/governance bullets. Tighten it around scope, platform leadership, and 1–2 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and analytics.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: combine “digital systems/workflows/analytics” with “governance/usability/operational best practices” into one stronger operations/governance bullet.
- Make the Drupal bullet outcome-led: mention campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits only if tied to speed, reuse, or engagement.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, publishing teams enabled, workflow time reduced, search relevance gains, or campaign launch speed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects “AI Hybrid Search”; keep one high-level here and save technical detail for the project section.
- Drupal microsite/storytelling language overlaps with “We Are Counties Microsite” in the footer.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles. Lead with transformation, systems, and enterprise ownership.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s enterprise digital ecosystem—web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget—leading a cross-functional team and organization-wide digital strategy.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific or measurable: include email list size, engagement growth, campaign results, production volume, or cost/time savings from the in-house studio.
- Tighten the analytics/governance bullets: “Built reporting stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making”; “Established publishing standards and cross-department workflows to strengthen governance and planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: editorial operations, newsletters, advocacy video, and cross-team coordination.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting editorial planning and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcome language: “Launched/expanded a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger verbs and, if possible, metrics: “Standardized publishing workflows and editorial coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and turnaround time.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” repeats the Director role; emphasize execution/coordination here, not team-wide leadership.
- “weekly advocacy video update” also appears in the 2015–2018 role/footer; frame this as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and work experience. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior leadership scope rather than generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:  
  • Enterprise digital strategy  
  • Editorial governance and content operations  
  • Cross-channel communications leadership  
  • Public-sector digital communications  
  • Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “digital communications” or “content operations” to better match the CV’s platform/governance emphasis.
- Keep terms parallel and noun-based; avoid broad phrases like “audience-focused,” which read softer than the rest of the CV.
- If space allows, make one skill more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise content governance for high-volume publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header/core competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is also echoed in core competencies; consider using this slot for “content operations” or “journey design” instead.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, not every individual technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)”
- Replace low-signal phrasing with impact-oriented language: “CMS modernization and front-end implementation” instead of listing “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” in full
- Keep only skills most supported by recent roles/projects: “API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search experiences”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) - CMS modernization and front-end implementation - API integrations and workflow automation - Airtable-based content systems - AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” and coding languages are already detailed in “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same level of granularity here.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies/header language; keep wording consistent but not repetitive.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize business impact and decision support.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than just platform names.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” then “KPI framework development, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: replace “KPI design” with “KPI framework development” and “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and reporting.”
- Optional rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and reporting • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly; keep this topline version more strategic and let the technical section hold the full tool inventory.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value delivery capabilities tied to recent leadership work, not tool-level tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production workflows”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect seniority and studio leadership.
- Shorten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid event delivery” unless virtual events are a major target role requirement.
- If space allows, add scale/context instead of a generic term, e.g. “Livestream production for advocacy and member events.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- Tool-level detail like “PTZ camera systems” may be better placed only in Technical + IT unless central to target roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS platforms or add light context that signals level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize most relevant platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to Coding/Technical Implementation or drop it if usage was limited.
- If space allows, add proficiency context instead of a pure list: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and better alignment with the rest of the CV.
- Keep this section platform-focused; avoid adding modernization/integration language already covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one a shorter technical inventory.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so don’t over-explain it here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and modern tools most aligned with recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Reorder for relevance/recency: **JavaScript • HTML5/CSS3 • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery**
- Consider adding scope/context if true: **JavaScript (front-end enhancements), API integrations, GTM implementation, edge scripting with Cloudflare Workers, CI/CD with GitHub Actions**
- If space allows, replace older/generic terms with stronger specificity: e.g., **Custom front-end development • Tag management • Edge/serverless scripting • Deployment automation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “API integrations” and technical execution themes also overlap with Core Competencies/Topline Skills; this section should stay tool-specific, not conceptual.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more category-led.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp”
- Move collaboration tools out unless central to systems work; Slack, Teams fit better under a broader “Collaboration Tools” item or can be dropped.
- If accurate, add scope/strength signal in parentheses: “Airtable (system design), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automation), Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project workflow management)”
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Project Systems” for clearer alignment with recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; keep all only if you’ve used each meaningfully.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this line should emphasize platform breadth and avoid repeating “email/newsletters” language.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **CRM, Email & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one capability cue for specificity: **campaign automation, segmentation, and member communications**
- Keep it concise and platform-focused rather than describing outcomes here; the impact is already better shown in recent NACo experience

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding phrases like “managed newsletters” or “reaching tens of thousands” here
- “Engagement” may feel vague unless paired with “CRM” or “member communications,” especially given the association/public-sector context

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs or scale if you can.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce channel list repetition: focus on website refresh, livestream/video production, and workflow support.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, event size, publishing volume, or team size supported.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving production workflows and day-to-day execution for web and multimedia communications. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided informal supervision and training to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if kept here, position it as launching or piloting the format.
- Avoid repeating broad “web, email, social” coverage already emphasized in later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and trim generic “coordinated/contributed” phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Recast to foreground the unique achievement: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research, project coordination, and digital storytelling.”
- Make the podcast launch the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten multimedia language: replace “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific outcome or channel if possible.
- If available, add scope: number of episodes, audiences reached, programs supported, or types of research/projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid overemphasizing broad digital leadership here; save that narrative for the more recent NACo roles.
